content.text:
“Clean gold” is usually called **fine gold** or **24-karat gold**, and **99.9% purity** means the metal is **999 parts gold out of 1,000**.

It is 99.9% rather than 100% because **absolute 100% purity is practically impossible** in real-world refining and measurement. Tiny amounts of other elements can remain, such as silver, copper, iron, or other trace metals. Even highly refined gold may contain microscopic impurities from ore, refining equipment, chemicals, or handling.

Also, **99.9% is a standard commercial purity grade**. In bullion markets it is often written as:

- **999 gold**
- **.999 fine gold**
- **24K gold**, though technically 24K is often used for very high-purity gold, not mathematically perfect gold

Some gold is refined even further, such as **99.99%**, written as **9999 fine gold**, but 99.9% is already considered very pure for many uses.

So the short answer is: **clean gold is 99.9% pure because refining can remove almost all impurities, but not literally every atom of non-gold material, and 99.9% is a widely accepted purity standard.**
